rule: Owner decision on #219 (2026-10-07): each dive draws its own seed at its start and keeps it in randomState, so a resumed dive stays deterministic; the shark's spawn and exit distances follow the wreck camera's lead, so it appears just outside the visible edge. The second is recorded in docs/decisions.md as a departure from legacy's centred view.
change: src/app/dive-seed.ts draws the seed from crypto.getRandomValues, and createWreckInitialState() starts each dive on it. src/app/game-controller.ts hands advanceWithBuoyancy() a DiveEnvironment.shark every frame: the clock's rate with fast-forward, the diver's swim along the route per dive second, the view to either side from wreckViewAround() (src/render/camera.ts: the 8 m lead and the camera's bound), the floor from floorUnder() (src/sites/wreck-route.ts) at the shark's position and depth, and the wreck's noShark. SharkFrame's viewHalfWidthM becomes viewLeftM and viewRightM, and its floorM a floorAt(offsetM, depthM) read after the swim. src/render/pixi-renderer.ts draws legacy's shark (src/renderer.js 1069-1124) once in the fauna layer and moves it each frame while DiveState.shark.encounter exists. The migration e2e specs (tests/helpers/pinned-seed.cjs) and scripts/pixi-visual-check.mjs pin the page's 32-bit draws to the seed the client used before, 0x57524543, so no run meets a shark by chance.

counterChecks.method: Each mutation applied by a script to a file backed up beforehand, the named tests run (for e2e, after rebuilding the client) under the port lock with --retries=0, on the code of d4a9780. Each file was then restored from its backup and compared with filecmp (shallow=False): byte for byte identical in every case. The first versions of the M7 and M8 mutations did not typecheck, so their builds failed before any e2e ran; the e2e results below are from the typechecking forms, void this.#sharkFrame(...) and drawDiveSeed() * 0 + 0x57524543.
